memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the priest shall sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from their uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering and offer it on the altar, together with the grain offering, and make atonement for them, and they will be clean." - Lev 14:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And they will be clean. After everything — the birds, the washing, the shaving, the waiting, the blood, the oil — it comes to rest on those five words.

Notice how definite they are. Not "they may hope to be clean." Not "they will feel clean." God declares the outcome.

That certainty is the great gift. This person did not walk away from the tabernacle wondering where they stood. The offerings had been made, atonement had been accomplished, and God said the word. Clean.

Yet notice something else, and let it stir a longing in you. All of this happened for one person, on one day. Next year, if the disease returned, it would all have to happen again. Hebrews puts its finger on the ache: those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins, because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins (Heb 10:3-4).

Then comes the contrast. But when this priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God (Heb 10:12). He sat down — the work was finished.

You will never need this chapter's ceremony. Christ has done it. You are clean, and He is seated.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live with assurance, or with lingering uncertainty about your standing?
2. What does it mean to you that Christ sat down when the work was done?
3. Whose word about you do you trust most — your own, or God's?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You offered one sacrifice for all time and then sat down. I rest in Your finished work and receive Your verdict over me: clean. Amen.
